summary: The Department responded to concerns about open/closed status by clarifying that the final statement and regulations now include three specific designation classes (open, restricted, closed) and that the pre-existing status of each bureau's lands would remain unchanged; it also addressed noise standards by noting ongoing cooperation with EPA and other agencies to develop Federal noise standards, while acknowledging insufficient data for a final decision at this time.
text:
2. Open-until-closed vs. closed-until-open policy regarding use of Federal lands for ORV
There were several incoming comments which questioned the current status of Interior lands regarding use of ORV, and suggested that the statement be clarified on this matter.
In response to these suggestions, the Department has included in both the final environmental statement and in its ORV regulations specific provisions establishing designation criteria and classes of designations applicable to ORV use or non-use of Interior lands. The three classes of designations are: (a) open use areas and trails where off-road vehicles may be operated without restrictions, but subject to the operating regulations and vehicle standards set forth in the regulations; (b) restricted areas and trails where the use of off-road vehicles is subject to restrictions, which may limit the numbers or types of vehicles allowed, times of use, and types of use; and (c) closed areas and trails where the use of off-road vehicles is permanently or temporarily prohibited. Part I(4)(a) of the final environmental statement provides specific use criteria for the designation or non-designation of areas and trails for ORV. Further, the ORV regulations define more specifically the designation criteria.
The general status of ORV use on Interior lands will remain the same as it was prior to the issuance of Executive Order 11644, i.e., lands under the jurisdiction of the National Park Service, the Bureau of Reclamation, and the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife will remain closed to ORV use unless otherwise designated, and those of the Bureau of Land Management will remain open to ORV use unless otherwise designated.
